Superior Court of San Joaquin

The Superior Court of San Joaquin is a cornerstone of the judicial system in San Joaquin County, California. Located at 180 E Weber Ave, Stockton, CA 95202, this court serves as a vital resource for resolving legal disputes, offering a wide range of services, and ensuring justice is served fairly and efficiently. Whether you're dealing with traffic tickets, family law matters, or criminal cases, the Superior Court of San Joaquin provides accessible and customer-oriented services to meet your needs.

Key Information About the Superior Court of San Joaquin

  • Address: 180 E Weber Ave, Stockton, CA 95202
  • Google Maps: Directions to Superior Court of San Joaquin
  • Working Hours:
    • Monday to Friday: 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM
    • Saturday & Sunday: Closed
  • Website: San Joaquin Superior Court Official Website

About the Superior Court of San Joaquin

Established in 1850, the Superior Court of San Joaquin has a rich history of serving the community. The current courthouse, built in 2017, features 30 modern courtrooms designed by NBBJ. The court’s mission is to resolve disputes fairly, consistently, and efficiently while promoting public confidence and providing a safe, respectful environment for all.

The court has jurisdiction over a variety of cases, including:

  • Criminal
  • Civil
  • Family Law
  • Juvenile
  • Traffic and Vehicle Violations
  • Small Claims
  • Probation

Services Offered by the Superior Court of San Joaquin

The court provides a wide range of services to make legal processes more accessible:

  1. Online Case Search: Search for case information by case number, party name, or filing year.
  2. Online Payments: Pay traffic tickets, fines, and fees through the Superior Court Online Portal.
  3. Self-Help Center: Resources for individuals representing themselves in court.
  4. Attorney Contact Registration: Register as an attorney to access case information and file documents.
  5. Remote Hearings: Available for family law and other cases.
  6. DUI Prevention Programs: Educational initiatives like "Choices and Consequences" to reduce impaired driving.

How to Search for Case Information

You can access case records online through the San Joaquin County Superior Court Case Management System. Search by:

  • Case Number
  • Party Name (First, Middle, Last)
  • Filing Year

Note: Some records may be confidential or unavailable online. In such cases, visit the courthouse to request access.

How to Make Payments

Payments for traffic tickets, fines, and fees can be made:

  1. Online: Visit www.ncourt.com and enter your citation or case number.
  2. In-Person: Visit the courthouse during business hours. Accepts cash, checks, and cards (2.5% surcharge for credit cards).
  3. By Mail: Send a certified check or money order to:
    180 E Weber Ave, Ste 203, Stockton, CA 95202

Court Locations and Divisions

The Superior Court of San Joaquin operates multiple branches across the county:

  1. Stockton Courthouse
    • Handles family law, civil, and criminal cases.
  2. Juvenile Justice Center
    • Focuses on dependency, delinquency, and traffic cases involving juveniles.
  3. Lodi Branch
    • Departments L-1 and L-2 handle criminal and traffic cases.
  4. Manteca Branch
    • Deals with civil harassment, traffic, criminal, and eviction cases.

Judges of the Superior Court of San Joaquin

The court is presided over by a team of experienced judges, including:

  • Robert Waters
  • Elizabeth Humphreys
  • Michael J. Mulvihill
  • Richard Vlavianos
  • Lauren P. Thomasson
  • And more

These judges are appointed by the Governor of California and are dedicated to upholding justice and fairness in all cases.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

  1. How do I file a small claims case?
    • Small claims cases (up to $10,000) are handled at the Lodi Branch.
  2. What happens if I don’t pay my fine on time?
    • Additional fines, license suspension, or warrants may be issued.
  3. Can I resolve my traffic citation online?
    • Yes, some cases are eligible for Online Dispute Resolution.
  4. What services does the Family Law Facilitator provide?
    • Free legal advice and consultations for those who cannot afford an attorney.
  5. How do I register as an attorney?
    • Complete the Attorney Contact Registration form online with your Bar number, contact information, and law firm details.

Programs and Initiatives

The Superior Court of San Joaquin is committed to community outreach and education. Key programs include:

  • Youth Programs: Educating young people about the legal system.
  • Restorative Justice: Alternative dispute resolution methods.
  • DUI Prevention: School-based programs to highlight the consequences of impaired driving.

Future of the Superior Court of San Joaquin

The court is continuously evolving to meet the needs of the community. Plans include:

  • Expanding facilities
  • Modernizing processes
  • Investing in technology to improve access to justice

Conclusion

The Superior Court of San Joaquin is a trusted institution dedicated to providing fair and efficient legal services to the residents of San Joaquin County. With its comprehensive range of services, experienced judges, and commitment to community outreach, the court ensures that justice is accessible to all. For more information, visit the official website or contact the court directly.
